## Antibody RFD3

Generate alternative antibody CDR backbone conformations while preserving the framework and antigen.

### Public interface guidance

Generate alternative antibody CDR backbone conformations with AgCDR-Diff, conditioned on an antibody–antigen structure. Supply separate antibody and antigen PDB files positioned in the same coordinate frame. The model samples CDR geometry while using the surrounding complex as structural context.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: agcdr_diff. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `antibody_pdb_path` | string | Required | file | Antibody PDB containing a numberable heavy chain and, for a paired antibody, a light chain. Its coordinates must already be positioned relative to the supplied antigen; this step does not dock the two inputs. |
| `antigen_pdb_path` | string | Required | file | Protein antigen PDB containing valid protein ATOM records. Use the same coordinate frame as the antibody structure. |
| `num_samples` | integer | Required | value | Number of CDR backbone conformations to sample. Enter an integer from 1 through 100. |
| `num_steps` | integer | Required | value | Number of diffusion sampling steps per sample. Enter an integer from 2 through 100; 50 is the standard setting. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: Generated complex PDB structures, the input reference and generation reports. The output describes CDR backbone conformations; amino-acid sequence design is a separate step.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `agcdr_diff`.

## RF-Antibody

Generate antibody or nanobody sequences from antibody and antigen structures.

### Public interface guidance

Generate antibody or nanobody designs against an antigen using the RFantibody workflow, followed by ProteinMPNN sequence design. Supply an appropriate framework structure and antigen structure, then select the antibody type and requested design count.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: rfdiffusion_proteinmpnn. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `antibody_pdb_path` | string | Required | file | Uploaded antibody or nanobody framework PDB used to condition design. Supply the structure file rather than a PDB accession alone. |
| `antigen_pdb_path` | string | Required | file | Uploaded target antigen PDB structure. Use the actual structure file, not a bare structure identifier. |
| `num_sequences` | integer | Required | value | Requested design count. Enter a positive integer; the default is 10. Check the delivered sequence count in the result archive. |
| `antibody_type` | string | Required | value | Select antibody for a paired heavy/light framework or nanobody for a heavy-chain-only framework. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: A ZIP of the ProteinMPNN-stage outputs. Inspect the included sequences, structures and any available metrics before selecting candidates for further evaluation.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `rfdiffusion_proteinmpnn`.

## Target-Aware CDR Designer / Epitope Conditioned Antibody Generation

Generate antigen- and epitope-conditioned antibody CDR backbones.

### Public interface guidance

Generate antibody CDR backbone conformations conditioned on an antigen epitope using Epitope AbGen/AbsciDiff. Supply antigen and antibody framework PDB structures, identify their chains, and select the CDR regions to regenerate. The remaining structure provides context for the sampled loops.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: epitope_abgen. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `antigen_pdb_path` | string | Required | file | Antigen PDB containing valid protein ATOM records and the chains carrying the selected epitope. |
| `antibody_pdb_path` | string | Required | file | Antibody framework PDB containing the heavy and light chains used to condition CDR generation. |
| `mask_cdrs` | string | Required | value | CDR regions to regenerate: hcdr3 for heavy-chain CDR3, heavy_cdrs for all heavy-chain CDRs, or all_cdrs for heavy- and light-chain CDRs. |
| `heavy_chain_id` | string | Required | value | Actual heavy-chain identifier in the antibody PDB. |
| `light_chain_id` | string | Required | value | Actual light-chain identifier in the antibody PDB. This paired-antibody workflow requires the corresponding light-chain structure. |
| `antigen_chain_ids` | array | Required | value | Identifiers of the antigen chains to include. Every selected chain must exist in antigen_pdb_path. For API requests, send a JSON array of chain IDs, such as ["A","C"]. |
| `epitope_residues` | array | Required | value | Antigen residues defining the desired interface. Identify each residue by its antigen chain and original PDB residue number, for example C:23 and C:24. For API requests, send a JSON array containing one chain-qualified residue per entry, such as ["C:23","C:24"]. |
| `samples_per_task` | integer | Required | value | Number of structures to sample for each prepared task. Enter an integer from 1 through 16; the default is 4. |
| `seed` | integer | Required | value | Random seed controlling sampling. Enter an integer from 0 through 4294967295; the default is 2026. Identical seeds do not guarantee identical results across software or hardware versions. |
| `max_tokens` | integer | Required | value | Model sequence-token budget. Enter an integer from 32 through 416; the default is 384. This controls the modeling budget, not the number of output samples. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: Generated PDB structures and accompanying reports. The outputs are CDR backbone conformations; final antibody sequence design is a separate step.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `epitope_abgen`.

| `complex_id` | string | no / mode-dependent | value | Omitted: defaults to platform-assigned experiment_id; never invent an experiment ID. |
| `mask_cdrs` | string | no / mode-dependent | value | User-selected scalar string from the form; do not send the UI wrapper object. |
| `epitope_residues` | array | no / mode-dependent | value | Array of user-supplied strings, as emitted by the recorded form. |

## AntiBMPNN

Generate structure-conditioned antibody sequence variants for selected chains or residue positions in an antibody or antibody-antigen structure.

### Public interface guidance

Generate antibody-chain amino-acid sequence variants conditioned on a backbone structure using AntiBMPNN. Supply an antibody or antibody–antigen structure, identify the chains to redesign and choose the number of samples. Structural conditioning helps retain the supplied backbone context during sequence design.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: AntiBMPNN. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `input_path` | string | Required | file | One antibody or antibody–antigen PDB, or a ZIP of PDB structures. Every chain selected for redesign must be present in each applicable structure. Only PDB members are processed. |
| `chains_to_design` | array | Required | value | Identifiers of the antibody chains whose sequences should be redesigned, such as H and L. Supply an explicit, non-empty selection without duplicates; each selected chain must exist in the structure. For API requests, send a non-empty JSON array of one-character chain IDs, such as ["H","L"]. |
| `generation_count` | integer | Required | value | Number of sequence samples per input PDB. Enter an integer from 1 through 10000. Duplicate sequences may occur. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product-interface limits (not overrides of connector validation): Request 1–10000 sequence samples per PDB. Chain selection must be non-empty and every selected chain must exist in the corresponding structure.

Product result guidance: An archive of designed sequence records and run outputs. Sample count does not guarantee sequence uniqueness or improved antibody properties.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `AntiBMPNN`.

### Inputs

Fields below belong in `experiment_data`. The connector generates `experiment_name` unless the user supplies one.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input_path` | string | yes | file | Uploaded single `.pdb` antibody/complex structure or one `.zip` containing PDB structures. Raw sequences and local paths are invalid. |
| `chains_to_design` | array | yes | value | Non-empty list of one-character PDB chain IDs, for example `['H', 'L']`. Every chain must exist in every applicable input structure. |
| `residue_positions_to_design` | object | no / mode-dependent | value | Designed-chain IDs mapped to one-based residue selections such as `101-106,115,119-123`. Omit or send `{}` for full-chain design. |
| `generation_count` | integer | yes | value | Sequences to generate per PDB; accepted range 1–10000. Use a small count for validation. |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;
`file_or_value` supports either documented mode; `artifact` is an authorized upstream result reference.
Only local files require a new upload. Never infer input mode from a field name.
